assessment: The paper addresses an important unresolved mechanism of antibiotic resistance caused by a RNA-modifying enzyme Cfr, a protein that confers resistance to multiple ribosome-targeting antibiotics due to methylation of the rRNA residue A2503 on the large ribosomal subunit. Tsai et al. identify the mutational hotspots that increase Cfr activity and show how a single methyl group on A2503 can hamper the antibiotic binding. The paper is an important contribution to our understanding of antibiotic resistance and is of broad interest to readers in the field of antibiotic resistance, biochemistry, structural biology, and medicinal chemistry.
